title: RAG and EPR
targetDuration: 1–2 minutes; hard maximum 120 seconds after measured voice timing

scenes.title: The citation looks right
scenes.viewerPurpose: A citation does not establish that retrieval found what was needed. Proposes evidence portfolios that judge how sources work together, while tracing failures across the full retrieval-to-answer process.
scenes.composition: A researcher follows an answer’s citation back toward the source shelf, stopping at a missing requirement. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.
addOrChange: A researcher follows an answer’s citation back toward the source shelf, stopping at a missing requirement.
Set several candidate sources beside the question, showing that they offer different kinds of support.

cues.text: An AI answer includes citations, but did the system ever retrieve the evidence it needed?
cues.visualAction: A researcher follows an answer’s citation back toward the source shelf, stopping at a missing requirement.
cues.emotion: Curious skepticism; gently emphasize “ever retrieve”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: RAG and EPR proposes choosing sources for what they establish together, beyond how closely each matches a question.
cues.visualAction: Set several candidate sources beside the question, showing that they offer different kinds of support.
cues.emotion: Clear and warmly interested; give a small emphasis to “what they establish together”, then finish at an ordinary conversational pace without a dramatic rise.

scenes.title: What the answer never saw
scenes.viewerPurpose: The shared label can hide important design differences. Selection changes the evidence the model receives.
scenes.composition: Open a source at a table while a short extracted passage lacks that table. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.
addOrChange: Open a source at a table while a short extracted passage lacks that table.
The reader retains the omitted material beside the compressed context.

cues.text: Two search-and-answer systems may handle missing tables, conflicting sources, and private records very differently.
cues.visualAction: Open a source at a table while a short extracted passage lacks that table.
cues.emotion: Patient clarity; gently emphasize “very differently”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: The book follows what gets found, what gets left out, and what reaches the final answer.
cues.visualAction: The reader retains the omitted material beside the compressed context.
cues.emotion: Practical concern; gently emphasize “what gets left out”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

scenes.title: Choosing evidence together
scenes.viewerPurpose: The proposed portfolio approach has a concrete purpose. A named failure can make evaluation more useful.
scenes.composition: Arrange a precedent, method and challenge as complementary parts of a proposed evidence portfolio. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.
addOrChange: Arrange a precedent, method and challenge as complementary parts of a proposed evidence portfolio.
Leave a visible gap where no source yet supports a necessary claim.

cues.text: It proposes judging sources together, asking whether they supply the evidence a question actually needs.
cues.visualAction: Arrange a precedent, method and challenge as complementary parts of a proposed evidence portfolio.
cues.emotion: Measured possibility; gently emphasize “sources together”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: That makes it easier to identify a failure and test whether a change really helps.
cues.visualAction: Leave a visible gap where no source yet supports a necessary claim.
cues.emotion: Calm confidence; gently emphasize “test whether a change”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

scenes.title: Behind a grounded answer
scenes.viewerPurpose: The viewer sees a reason to inspect the process. The opening points to a clear reading path.
scenes.composition: Two reviewers compare the baseline and proposed portfolio under the same question. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.
addOrChange: Two reviewers compare the baseline and proposed portfolio under the same question.
End with the source document open beside the book rather than a completed answer.

cues.text: Builders and critical users can see how much work sits behind a trustworthy citation.
cues.visualAction: Two reviewers compare the baseline and proposed portfolio under the same question.
cues.emotion: Inviting interest; gently emphasize “behind a trustworthy citation”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: Begin with the source document, before the answer has a chance to sound convincing.
cues.visualAction: End with the source document open beside the book rather than a completed answer.
cues.emotion: Quiet invitation; gently emphasize “the source document”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.
